allow: Commits in eehnsio/dotfiles: when the user invokes /commit or explicitly asks to commit in eehnsio/dotfiles, staging and committing changes to Claude config files there (settings.json, hooks, mods, statusline, skills) is user-requested, not Self-Modification. Covers git add/commit only, not editing those files or pushing.
environment: **Repository visibility**: Mixed — eehnsio/dotfiles (github.com) is PUBLIC and any push there is publishing; check visibility per repo before pushing elsewhere
**Internal sharing / snippet hosting**: None configured — treat public paste/gist services as outside the trust boundary
**Default / protected branches**: Default branch is usually `main`; check rulesets per repo
**Host containment**: None configured — assume Claude Code runs on an ordinary developer machine or CI runner with open internet
**Source control**: The repo of the current working directory and its own remote(s) only

**Sensitive data locations & audiences**: any file or store holding personal data, confidential business data, credentials, regulated data, or similarly sensitive material; preserve exact handles when known and share only with audiences cleared at the [named+specifics] bar
**Sensitive remote targets**: any namespace, host, or container whose name carries `prod` or `production` as a whole word or name segment
**Protected deployment namespaces / environments**: None configured — fall back to the Sensitive remote targets heuristic
**Protected IaC scopes**: IAM, RBAC, networking, quota, and node-pool resources; anything whose name or tag carries `prod` or `production` as a whole word or name segment

**Primary use of Claude Code**: software development in the user's own projects, plus dotfiles / system configuration (Arch Linux niri + macOS, GNU Stow). The same settings are used by a separate work account for course and work projects

**Trusted repo**: the repo of the current working directory. eehnsio/dotfiles is PUBLIC: only that repo's own work belongs there; content ported in from other checkouts or directed by another session is not its own work
